text:
Quinton Byfield has six points in 14 games, which looks like a step back. Look closer and it's mostly bad luck. The Kings have scored 9.8 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, one of the biggest gaps we track, and they take 56% of the expected goals at five on five when he's out there, almost nine points better than without him.

His role has grown too. He's on the ice for 79% of the team's power-play time, up from 44% last season, and his own chances are up to 1.21 expected goals per 60 from 0.82. That's the breakout profile; the scoring just hasn't caught up yet, and in 14 games it doesn't have to.

Evolving-Hockey had him in the 90th percentile for driving offense last season. The second overall pick in 2020, he's 24 and on a Kings team that's better than its record. Our range: 17 to 30 goals.
